transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 14:00 - 14:38 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM), Samara Ortiz (Nimbus CTO), Ethan Mills (Platform Lead), Jae Kim (ML Eng), Rita Gomez (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick review of last week's benchmark, slight underprovision during spike at 03:20 UTC, discussed changing autoscale threshold and adding a small burst pool. Action items captured at the end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this to 30-ish minutes, quick review of the perf numbers and then dig into autoscale and burst, priya you want to start with the benchmark recap?
[00:12] Priya: Yeah sure, um, so last Wednesday we ran the 2-hour window sim across the 13B opt-like model, sequence 2k typical requests, and then a handful of 4k sequences for edge cases. Our p95 latency on dedicated nodes was about 220 ms per token under steady load, and during the spike window where customer traffic doubled we saw latency climb to 650 ms for a short period, that correlates with KV cache miss patterns and then our autoscaler reaction time which was roughly 90 seconds.
[00:40] Jae: sorry can I interrupt, the traffic we saw on the spike was largely from batch jobs kicking off, not user interactive, so we probably would prefer burst capacity rather than upscaling baseline which increases cost.
[00:52] Priya: totally makes sense, and that's what we wanted to discuss, adding a configurable burst pool that can be used for short tail spikes. currently the default autoscale policy does cool down for 2 minutes, we can shorten that but you pay in terms of more frequent scale events.
[01:10] Samara: just high level - our budget for Dedicated is sensitive; we want to avoid steady-state uplift. Burst sounds good but how do we get price visibility?
[01:18] Alex: Good question. We'll share a pricing sheet that splits baseline reserved capacity vs burst buffer costs and shows amortized per-token costs across typical vs peak. I'll send that after the call.
[01:27] Ethan: one more constraint - we have strict burst caps due to network egress and our infra team needs scheduling windows for large batch jobs; we can try to schedule them off-peak if the autoscaler is predictable.
[01:40] Priya: for autoscale rules, our recommendation is baseline at X replicas for steady throughput and then two scaling tiers: fast-burst tier (pre-warmed replicas) with immediate routing for 1-3 minutes, and a sustained-scale tier that scales up additional replicas with a 90-120s ramp. The math we used is in the spreadsheet: pre-warm cost is cheaper than constantly overprovisioning.
[02:05] Rita: from security standpoint, if you pre-warm we need to verify that those pre-warmed instances still comply with our VPC flow rules and that logs are retained per our policy. Are pre-warmed pools isolated per customer?
[02:16] Alex: yes, in Dedicated mode pools are tenant-isolated, and we can surface audit logs to your SIEM. we'll also enable KMS usage for model keys per the private deployment options.
[02:27] Rita: okay good. please add a line item in the compliance doc about pre-warm auditability.
[02:32] Maya: noted - we'll add a compliance note.
[02:35] Priya: back to the perf: the 4k sequences are the real cost driver. We saw 2.1x token generation time vs 2k seq in the same model. If those are a small portion of traffic, bursting pre-warms ahead of scheduled batch windows will help. Jae, do you have % of traffic that is >3k tokens?
[02:55] Jae: currently about 6% of requests are >3k, but those account for ~22% of total token volume, so they have outsized cost impact.
[03:05] Priya: ok that explains the spike. So recommended baseline supports 94% of normal traffic, and a pre-warm burst pool sized for the high-tail at about 20% additional capacity to handle those large sequences without pushing latency up.
[03:20] Ethan: operationally, can we set a scheduled window to pre-warm before the nightly batch? That would reduce costs if those batches are predictable.
[03:28] Priya: yes we support schedule-based pre-warm as well as reactive. schedule-based pre-warm avoids autoscale churn.
[03:34] Samara: what's the expected hit to our monthly committed spend if we add a 20% pre-warm?
[03:40] Alex: rough calc from the spreadsheet, on your current baseline it would be about +11-13% committed spend but lower per-token cost during spikes; with burst billing mode the amortized cost could be lower if bursts are short and infrequent. We'll send detailed line items.
[03:55] Jae: about the autoscaler sensitivity - is there a way to tune the cooldowns per route? We have a mix of short chat requests and long generative jobs.
[04:04] Priya: great question, yes we support per-route autoscale configs. For low-latency chat routes we use a faster reaction and smaller pre-warm pool, for long jobs we use scheduled pre-warm and larger batch windows.
[04:18] Ethan: any notes on GPU flavors? We tested on A100-like nodes in the POC; do we get benefit from switching to H100 for the 4k sequences?
[04:27] Priya: H100 will help for large batch/long sequences due to better memory bandwidth and faster attention kernels; however it's pricier. For Dedicated we can offer mixed pools - some H100 for heavy-long requests, and cheaper A100/80GB for baseline. That adds orchestration complexity but reduces average cost.
[04:44] Samara: mixed pools sounds promising but adds operational overhead for us. How mature is the routing policy? We need guaranteed routing for pinned customers during a rollout.
[04:54] Alex: routing is policy-driven; we can pin traffic to model variants and hardware tiers. Failover policies exist to move to compatible model quantized variant if heavy tier unavailable. We'll document that in the runbook.
[05:05] Priya: quick note on KV cache - most of the latency during the spike appears to be from cache misses. We can recommend a slightly higher memory allocation per core for your pre-warm pool to increase hit rate. That impacts instance selection.
[05:18] Jae: do you have numbers on cache hit improvement vs memory increase?
[05:21] Priya: in our internal tests a 20% memory bump improved hit rate by ~12% for similar request patterns, which translated to ~8-10% lower token latency on the tail. I'll include that data.
[05:33] Samara: on compliance again, we need to confirm retention policy for KV caches in Dedicated, and whether we can disable logging for certain workloads.
[05:41] Rita: disabling logging is tricky, but we might be able to reduce retention window for sensitive workloads and push logs to your SIEM. we'll follow up with a security addendum.
[05:52] Alex: sounds good. Quick operational ask: Ethan, can you share a 7-day hourly histogram of requests? that will let priya size the burst pool more precisely.
[05:58] Ethan: yes we can, will do - I think we can export from our metrics cluster. we'll aim for 2026-04-24.
[06:05] Priya: i'll walk through the autoscale spreadsheet now - giving examples: if baseline is 8 replicas and each replica handles 120 reqs/sec steady at 2k seq, scaling to 10 replicas buys you 25% more capacity; pre-warm pool of 2 replicas covers the high tail and can be allocated for immediate routing. We also model billing: pre-warm can be billed as reserved but with a burst discount.
[06:30] Alex: ok let's talk about benchmarking window - we propose a 2-hour bench with synthetic spikes to validate end-to-end latency and autoscale behavior, we'll need permission to run that during your maintenance window.
[06:43] Samara: maintenance window is typically 02:00-04:00 UTC, that should be fine.
[06:48] Jae: also want to run a config with H100 nodes for comparison, maybe run 30-minute H100 vs A100 to see cost/latency delta.
[06:56] Priya: yes we can do that, we'll include comparison metrics in the spreadsheet and a short summary doc.
[07:02] Alex: final recap before we wrap - action items and owners are in the notes. We'll deliver pricing breakdown, updated autoscale spreadsheet, and schedule the benchmark once Ethan uploads histograms. Any other blockers?
[07:14] Samara: none from me, just want the compliance note on pre-warm auditability.
[07:20] Rita: noted.
[07:22] Alex: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up by end of week.

End of transcript.
